pdm-pulmonary-function: What three things do pulmonary function tests measure?
Flow, volume and gas transfer
Which test is done in a glass booth?
Whole-body plethysmography
Which lung volume is the key measurement of whole-body plethysmography?
The residual volume
Besides lung volumes, what does whole-body plethysmography measure?
Airway resistance
Which device measures airflow and some lung volumes?
The spirometer
Which bedside or home device measures peak expiratory flow?
The peak flow meter
Peak expiratory flow correlates with which spirometry value?
The forced expiratory volume in one second
Which device measures gas exchange and oxygenation from a blood sample?
The blood gas analyzer
Which device's readout gives the pH and the oxygen and carbon dioxide partial pressures?
The blood gas analyzer
Which fingertip device measures oxygenation?
The pulse oximeter
Which tool calibrates a spirometer?
The calibration syringe
What is the air moved with each normal restful breath?
The tidal volume
About how large is the tidal volume?
About 500 mL
What is the extra volume breathed in on top of the tidal volume?
The inspiratory reserve volume
What is the extra volume breathed out after a normal breath out?
The expiratory reserve volume
Which volume can never be breathed out?
The residual volume
About how large is the residual volume?
Is a capacity one compartment or a sum of volumes?
A sum of volumes
Which two volumes make the inspiratory capacity?
Tidal volume + inspiratory reserve volume
Which two volumes make the functional residual capacity?
Expiratory reserve volume + residual volume
Which three volumes make the vital capacity?
Tidal + inspiratory reserve + expiratory reserve
Which volume does the vital capacity leave out?
The residual volume
Which capacity is the air left at the end of a quiet breath out?
The functional residual capacity
Which capacity is the maximum the lungs can hold?
The total lung capacity
About how large is the total lung capacity?
For at least how long does the patient exhale in spirometry?
6 seconds
How many times is the spirometry effort repeated?
3 times
Which spirometry efforts are recorded, per the slide?
The highest volumes and flows
What is the total volume forcefully exhaled after a maximal breath?
The forced vital capacity
What is the volume blown out in the first second?
The forced expiratory volume in one second
What percentage does the ratio express?
The share of the forced vital capacity exhaled in the first second
What is a normal ratio?
More than 80%
Below what ratio is obstruction indicated?
What are the three most important values in reading pulmonary function tests?
The forced vital capacity, the forced expiratory volume in one second and their ratio
What is the maximum velocity created during forced expiration?
The peak expiratory flow rate
Where is the peak expiratory flow on the flow-volume loop?
At the top of the expiratory limb
What is the average flow over the middle half of the forced vital capacity?
The forced expiratory flow 25% to 75%
On the volume-time curve, what does the plateau mark?
The forced vital capacity
On the flow-volume loop, which limb is above the axis?
The expiratory limb
What is the normal range, as percent of predicted, for the forced vital capacity?
What is the normal range, as percent of predicted, for the total lung capacity?
What is the most common reason to order pulmonary function tests?
To help diagnose a patient with a pulmonary symptom
Do pulmonary function tests give a specific diagnosis?
No: they show the derangement
Which long-term medication is screened for with pulmonary function tests?
Amiodarone
Before which surgery do pulmonary function tests estimate risk?
Lung resection
Into which three categories do pulmonary function tests classify diffuse lung disease?
Obstructive, restrictive and pulmonary vascular
Which pattern is trouble getting air OUT?
Obstructive
Which pattern is trouble getting air IN?
Restrictive
Which pattern is a decrease in volume?
Restrictive
Is bronchiectasis obstructive or restrictive?
Obstructive
Is scoliosis obstructive or restrictive?
Restrictive
Is sarcoidosis obstructive, restrictive or vascular?
It can be all three
How do neuromuscular diseases cause restriction?
Weakness of the respiratory muscles
Name a gas transfer impairment from the slides.
Pulmonary hypertension
In obstruction, which value falls below 70%?
The ratio
In restriction, which value is decreased?
The forced vital capacity
In restriction, what does the ratio do?
Stays normal or increases
What does an obstructive volume-time curve look like?
A slow rise and a long, late plateau
What does a restrictive volume-time curve look like?
The normal shape at a lower volume
"A scoop in the loop" means which pattern?
Obstruction
What is the scooped deformity of the expiratory limb called?
Coving
A loop shaped like a witch's hat means which pattern?
Restriction
Which film fits obstruction?
Hyperinflated lungs with flat diaphragms
Which value do you assess first on a report?
The ratio
Low ratio and low total lung capacity reads as what?
A mixed defect
Normal ratio with a low forced vital capacity suggests what?
Possible restriction
Which standard test diagnoses obstructive disease?
Spirometry with the flow-volume loop
Which standard test diagnoses restrictive disease?
Lung volumes
Which standard test diagnoses pulmonary vascular disease?
The diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide
What does the diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide measure?
The integrity of the alveolar-capillary membrane
Which test monitors response to treatment as well as prognosis?
The six-minute walk test
Which test checks oxygenation at rest and with modest activity?
Exercise oximetry
Is the arterial blood gas a standard or a specialized test?
Specialized
Which specialized test measures diaphragmatic strength?
Maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressures

Air left after a quiet breath out
The most the lungs can hold
